analysis:
Examined the ProviderLoop+Serve.swift changes (head lines 493 and 519) and the ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift hunk (head ~302-308). The PR makes three changes. (1) Shutdown now includes selectedModelRecovery.attempt?.task in the preloads list at Serve.swift:493, so it is cancelled and awaited via waitForPreloads with the bounded timeout. (2) The inline unload loop is replaced by unloadAllModelsForShutdown() at Serve.swift:519. The base loop waited for in-flight unloads and called unloadModel for every slot until modelSlots was empty. The helper's body is not supplied, so I cannot confirm it keeps that semantics (waits for modelsUnloading, loops until empty). If it did not, model weights and KV state could linger after shutdown (T-028, T-041 residual data), but that is an unverified contract, not evidence of a regression. (3) After the startup preload gate, enqueueSelectedModelRecovery is invoked only when not cancelled, not shutting down and startupPreloadStopRequested is false.

This introduces a background model-load retry path (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery, not supplied). Items for the next pass: whether recovery loads respect the add-on hold and servingDrain.refusingForServiceChange (T-059, A-018); whether they respect memory protection and the weight-hash verification and advertisement gates (T-027, T-012); whether a recovery load can race registration or the advertised set built at Serve.swift:180; and whether the recovery task is reliably cancelled on the drain and shutdown paths other than the main run() tail. The shutdown ordering is otherwise preserved: the coordinator is shut down, native MiMo owners are drained, then the models unload.

No changes to attestation, App Attest, key handling, the encryption paths or the coordinator wire contract. No concrete regression identified from the supplied evidence.
